title: Choose the look for Nadir
question: Clean, white, card grid with a side panel, as you asked. The roll assigned the Sale Catalogue. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Sale Catalogue
options.lineage: Auction-house sale catalogues: numbered lots, provenance, condition reports
options.thesis: Each week is a sale: strong companies come up as numbered lots, each with its record and a condition report on the fall.
options.viewport: A slim header naming this week's sale window, then a clean grid of numbered lot cards: lot number, company, the fall, the 3-year record, a one-year line.
options.risk: Catalogue wording turns twee if it goes past lot numbers and section names; the data must stay plain.

raised.raise: Filter tabs carry their counts, so each section's size reads before you open it.
The sale date (the five-session window) anchors the page like the date on a catalogue cover.
Numbers refresh in place in fixed-width figures; nothing reflows when prices update.
Monochrome discipline: black, grey and white carry everything; red is spent only on falls.
Every lot card shares one identical label grid, so the same number sits in the same spot on every card.

options.label: The Annual Report
options.thesis: Nadir as an annual report: one big figure per card, a strict grid, one sentence explaining each number.
options.viewport: Header, then a grid of cards led by an oversized percentage, with the company and a single explanatory sentence beneath.
options.risk: The most familiar clean-finance look; tidy, but close to what many dashboards already ship.

options.label: Acetate Manual Tabs
options.lineage: Boxed-software manuals with coloured tab dividers
options.thesis: Sections as coloured tab boards with clear acetate leaves.
options.viewport: A tab rail down the edge, one saturated board per sector.
options.case: Loses on clarity: full-strength colour boards fight a clean white scan.
options.risk: Loud and heavy for a daily check.

options.label: Wall Calendar Pad
options.thesis: A painted plate above a tear-off date pad.
options.viewport: A big illustration over a week pad.
options.case: Loses both: no real imagery to paint, and time is not Nadir's only axis.
options.kept: The week window anchors the page.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: Stocks as departures on a clacking flap board.
options.viewport: A dark board of rows flipping on update.
options.case: Loses on audience fit: dark board contradicts the white-mode brief.
options.risk: Gimmick once the flip novelty fades.
options.kept: Figures refresh in place without reflow.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Pure black-and-white data fields and barcodes.
options.viewport: A wall of bars with numbers in the margins.
options.case: Loses on clarity: art, not a tool friends can read.
options.kept: Monochrome discipline; red only for falls.

options.label: Gravity-Rain Garden
options.thesis: Rain that falls toward coloured clouds.
options.case: Loses both: no relationship to investing.

options.label: Sneaker Box Wall
options.thesis: Stocks as labelled boxes you pull from a wall.
options.viewport: A wall of box ends with labels.
options.case: Loses on audience fit; orange board fights white mode.
options.kept: One identical label grid on every card.

canonCard.label: The broker-app standard
canonCard.thesis: What stock apps ship: white cards, green and red numbers, system font, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: A watchlist-style card grid with ticker, price and change.
canonCard.risk: Clean but interchangeable with every broker app.
